essentials: The PPWR sets **directly applicable rules for all packaging** on the EU market, replacing a directive that Member States had implemented very differently.
By **2030 all packaging must be recyclable**, plastic packaging must contain **minimum shares of recycled material**, and empty space in shipping boxes is limited.
It applies in general since **12 August 2026**; most design requirements follow in **2030**.
Every company that packs products or sells packed products in the EU is affected, in different roles.

sections.title: Why it exists
text: Packaging waste per person in the EU has kept growing, and recycling has not kept up. Under the 1994 Packaging Directive each Member State wrote its own rules, so companies faced 27 sets of labelling and registration requirements. The PPWR replaces this with one regulation covering the whole life cycle of packaging, from design to waste.

sections.title: Design requirements
points: **Recyclability.** From 2030 packaging must be designed for recycling and is graded A, B or C. Packaging below grade C, that is less than 70% recyclable, may no longer be placed on the market. From 2035 it must also be recycled at scale in practice.

**Recycled content in plastic packaging.** From 2030: 30% for contact-sensitive packaging made of PET, 10% for other contact-sensitive plastic packaging, 30% for single-use plastic beverage bottles and 35% for other plastic packaging. The shares rise in 2040.
**Minimisation.** Weight and volume must be reduced to the minimum needed. For grouped, transport and e-commerce packaging the empty space may not exceed 50%.
**Substances.** Limits on heavy metals continue, and since 12 August 2026 food-contact packaging may not contain PFAS above set thresholds.
**Compostability.** Required for a few items such as tea bags and fruit stickers; otherwise not a route around recyclability.

sections.title: Reduction, reuse and bans
points: **Waste reduction targets** for Member States: packaging waste per person down 5% by 2030, 10% by 2035 and 15% by 2040, compared with 2018.
**Reuse targets** for 2030, for example for transport packaging and beverages, with exemptions.

**Restricted formats** from 2030: certain single-use plastic packaging, such as for fresh fruit and vegetables under 1.5 kg, for food and drink consumed on the premises in restaurants, single portions of condiments, and miniature toiletries in hotels.
**Take-away**: businesses must let customers bring their own container.
**Deposit return systems** for single-use plastic bottles and metal cans by 2029, unless a Member State already reaches very high collection rates.

sections.title: Labelling and information
text: Harmonised labels showing material composition, to help consumers sort waste, become mandatory in August 2028, with matching labels on waste bins. Reusable packaging gets its own label. National labelling requirements that conflict with the harmonised system have to go. Environmental claims about packaging are allowed only for features that exceed the legal minimum.

sections.title: Enforcement
text: Manufacturers must hold technical documentation and issue an EU declaration of conformity for their packaging. Market surveillance authorities check compliance and can order non-compliant packaging off the market. Producers must be registered in each Member State where they sell; without registration, packaging may not be made available there. Penalties are set nationally.

mistakes.wrong: The PPWR only concerns packaging manufacturers.
mistakes.right: Anyone who packs products, imports packed goods or sells online into a Member State has duties.
The general framework does. Recyclability, recycled content and format bans mostly start in 2030, labelling in 2028.
Compostability is required only for a few items. Everything else must be recyclable.

mistakes.wrong: One registration covers the whole EU.
mistakes.right: Producer registration and fees remain national.
All materials are covered. Some targets, such as recycled content, are specific to plastic.

practice: **List all packaging** you use or sell, by material, weight and function.
**Determine your role** per product and per Member State.
**Check registration and EPR** in every country you sell into, including online sales.
**Test recyclability** against the design-for-recycling criteria as they are published, and plan redesigns before 2030.
**Secure recycled plastic supply**; demand will exceed supply as 2030 approaches.
**Measure empty space** in shipping packaging and adjust box sizes.

quiz.q: What is the main structural change of the PPWR compared with the old Packaging Directive?
options: It applies directly in all Member States as a regulation
quiz.why: The directive led to 27 national regimes. The regulation harmonises most rules, though producer registration stays national.

options: Packaging must be at least 70% recyclable to be placed on the market
All packaging must be made of recycled material
Only glass and paper are allowed
quiz.why: Packaging must reach at least grade C, 70% recyclable. Lower-performing packaging is barred from the market.

quiz.q: What is the minimum recycled content for general plastic packaging from 2030?
quiz.why: 35% for plastic packaging that is not contact-sensitive or a beverage bottle. Contact-sensitive packaging has lower minimums.

quiz.q: What is the maximum empty space allowed in e-commerce packaging?
quiz.why: The empty space ratio for grouped, transport and e-commerce packaging may not exceed 50%.

quiz.q: Which restriction has applied since 12 August 2026?
options: The ban on single-use plastic packaging for fruit
Limits on PFAS in food-contact packaging
quiz.why: PFAS limits apply from the general start date. Format bans follow in 2030, labels in 2028, deposit systems by 2029.

quiz.q: An online shop in one Member State ships packed goods to consumers in three others. Where is it a ‘producer’?
options: In each Member State where it first makes the packaging available
Only where it has a warehouse
quiz.why: The producer role is defined per Member State, so registration and fees can be due in each country served.
